title: Review: relay_queue cleanup_orphan predicate fix
notes:
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — inconsistent idiom between the two startup scan functions is the main vector; a contributor copy-pastes the wrong predicate style. Security surface is low (local filesystem only).
Confidence: 15% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: if9z.1 (non-UTF-8 paths are a theoretical concern on Linux where filenames can contain arbitrary bytes — practically the queue dir is written by this code so filenames are always ASCII). Uncertainty driven by: cannot see other callers of cleanup_tmp_files or how the queue dir might be externally modified. Would raise confidence if: integration test with a non-UTF-8 filename in the queue dir.
Idiom rating: CLEAN — the changed predicate (path.extension().is_some_and(|e| e == 'msg')) is idiomatic Rust; correct OsStr comparison via PartialEq<str>, no allocations, no unsafe. The surrounding function is idiomatic. The only idiom concern is the unchanged cleanup_tmp_files using to_str() which was already captured as a P1 maintainer-burden finding.
Rust idiom confidence: 90% chance of no missed issue. Least confident flags: none in the changed code itself. Uncertainty driven by: async read_dir behavior across platforms not exercised by the test suite.
